solution:
Integrate $f''(x)=a$ twice:
$$f'(x)=ax+b, \qquad f(x)=\tfrac12ax^2+bx+c.$$

From $f(0)=1$ we get $c=1$. From $f(1)=2$,
$$\tfrac12a+b+1=2 \quad\Rightarrow\quad a+2b=2. \tag{1}$$

From the integral condition,
$$\int_0^1 f(x)\,dx=\left[\tfrac16ax^3+\tfrac12bx^2+x\right]_0^1=\tfrac16a+\tfrac12b+1=1,$$
so $\tfrac16a+\tfrac12b=0$, i.e.
$$a+3b=0. \tag{2}$$

Subtracting (1) from (2): $b=-2$. Then (1) gives $a+2(-2)=2$, so $a=6$.

The answer is **F**.
hints: Integrate f''(x)=a twice to get f(x) in terms of a, b, c.
Use f(0)=1 and f(1)=2 to get two equations.
Use the integral condition for a third equation and solve.
